[]` in createEvent, createAttendees, updateEvent, and deleteEvent, and its createEvent signature takes no credentialId, while GoogleCalendarService.createEvent explicitly gained `credentialId: number` and does `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. EventManager's new createAllCalendarEvents loop iterates all destinationCalendar entries per credential, so a multi-Lark-host collective booking would pass the same evt to each Lark credential, and every call would resolve the first host's externalId regardless of the credential — the per-credential targeting fix is only implemented for Google. Mechanism is visible in the diff; the practical failure mode depends on runtime behavior, so confidence is moderate.

judged_text: createEvent (and the createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent fallbacks) read only destinationCalendar[0]'s externalId, so for a multi-host collective event every per-credential call targets the first host's Lark calendar regardless of which member's credential is authenticated. A collective booking with two Lark hosts makes host B's authenticated createEvent call write to host A's calendarId (failing or duplicating) while host B's destination calendar never receives the event — the multi-host fix is implemented only for Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now loops over each destination calendar and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, only Google’s `createEvent` uses the passed credential context to select the matching destination calendar (`find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). In contrast, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent()` (and `createAttendees`, plus update/delete fallbacks when `externalCalendarId` is absent) destructure only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`). Since the provider call receives the full array (not a per-destination filtered event) and Lark doesn’t select by credential, each per-credential invocation can target `destinationCalendar[0]`’s externalId, matching the reported multi-host collective misrouting/duplication issue. This is directly verifiable in the Lark service code and the new multi-destination loop in EventManager.
